clue.text: A lot of switches in the same generator

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the abbreviation for ditto

parts.note: DO is the short form of ditto, meaning the same

indicators.note: switches here means changes direction, so the word for a lot is turned round

parts.note: a lot means many

explanation.surface: An electrician finds that many switches share one generator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switches' looks like a noun for electrical switches; here it is a verb, meaning turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a machine that produces electric current, a kind of generator.

clue.text: Filling in made me leave debate

indicators.note: the answer fills the inside of the following words, so it sits hidden within them

explanation.surface: Someone filling in for a colleague had to leave a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: The French borrowing, found in Chambers, means a quarrel or argument.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loanword means a dispute or contest, and a heated debate is such an argument.

clue.text: Gang space is rough isn't it?

parts.note: a nest can mean a gang, as in a nest of thieves

indicators.note: rough describes the letters of space as roughly handled and put in a new order

explanation.surface: A gang's hideout is in poor shape, isn't it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' rearranges SPACE into CEPAS. The French tag means 'isn't it?', asked to invite agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase is a tag question asking for agreement, exactly like the English 'isn't it?'.

clue.text: Jersey post collection

parts.note: post means letters delivered, mail
a lot is a collection of items, as at auction

explanation.surface: A batch of letters from the island of Jersey arrives together.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey looks like the Channel Island; it is a garment, notably a cyclist's jersey.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a tight top or vest worn by cyclists or dancers, a type of jersey.

clue.text: Go short to satisfy one's rebellious obsession

indicators.note: rebellious suggests revolting, turning over, so the assembled pieces are read backwards
short means the word for go loses its last letter

parts.note: to go is to exit
to satisfy hunger is to feed
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A rebel's obsession demands brief action to satisfy it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebellious' (revolting, turning over) turns the whole string of pieces round, not just one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means a fixed idea that dominates the mind, an obsession.

clue.text: I'll give you one, as an example

definitions.text: I'll give you one, as an example

parts.words: I'll give you one, as an example
parts.note: the cheeky reply 'I'll give you one' is a classic remark with a second, saucy meaning

explanation.walkthrough: The British phrase 'I'll give you one' is a familiar innuendo, a stock sexual quip, so the clue itself is an instance of what it defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived term names a phrase with two meanings, one usually risqué, which the quoted quip shows.

clue.text: Green produce extremely unusual as addition to dining table

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters are rearranged into a different form
extremely picks the extreme letters, the first and last, of produce

explanation.surface: Fresh green produce makes an unusual extra on the dinner table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives PE from produce; 'unusual' mixes it with GREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an ornamental centrepiece with branching dishes for fruit or flowers, placed on a dining table.

clue.text: Northern dwelling, one with good bathroom

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
loo is British slang for a toilet or bathroom

explanation.surface: A northern home with one good bathroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A snow-block house built by Inuit people in the Arctic is a dwelling of the far north.

clue.text: Danish city relies on train

indicators.note: to train something is to shape or direct it, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A Danish city depends on its rail service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like the railway, but it is the anagram signal on RELIES ON.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the English name for Helsingør, the Danish town of Hamlet's castle.

clue.text: One trying issue of Paris Match?

definitions.text: One trying issue of Paris Match?

parts.words: One trying issue of Paris Match?
parts.note: issue reads as child rather than magazine edition, trying as troublesome, and Paris Match points to French

explanation.walkthrough: Paris Match is a French magazine, so 'issue' looks like an edition; it is offspring, and 'trying' means difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase literally means terrible child, a person whose behaviour shocks or embarrasses.

clue.text: An African male in part of capital

parts.note: acting in the part of someone is acting as them
capital as an exclamation means excellent, A1, written here as AI

explanation.surface: An African man lives in one district of a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city, but it means first-rate, A1, with the 1 written as I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masai are a pastoral people of Kenya and Tanzania, so one of them is an African.

clue.text: Reason to guard against fashion magazine stories

indicators.note: to guard is to surround protectively, so one piece encloses the others

parts.note: nous is common sense or reason
V stands for versus, meaning against
Elle is a well-known fashion magazine

explanation.surface: There's good reason to keep a fashion magazine's gossip pieces at arm's length.
explanation.definitionFit: French for short stories or novellas; the borrowed term means tales of moderate length.

clue.text: Buzz Lightyear's complete opposite?

parts.note: buzz is a phone call and lightyear suggests huge distance, so the reverse is a nearby ring

explanation.walkthrough: Buzz Lightyear, the Toy Story spaceman, splits as 'buzz' (a ring on the phone) and 'light year' (a vast distance); the opposite of a light-year buzz is a nearby one.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone call to a nearby number is the reverse of one across a light year.

clue.text: Become monarch, breaking a habit

definitions.note: become is read as the past participle, as in 'has become'

indicators.note: breaking means splitting into the other word, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a habit is a robe or garment, like a gown
R is short for rex or regina, a monarch

explanation.surface: A nun leaves her order to become queen, breaking with her habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Become' is the past participle: 'has become' equals 'has grown'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have matured into something is the same sense of change; both participles describe having developed.

clue.text: Favourite thing of young Parisian right for breakfast

parts.note: a pet is a favourite
it can mean a thing
in French, of is de and young is jeune

explanation.surface: A young Parisian's favourite thing is said to be a proper breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian' signals that 'of young' is put into French: DE JEUNE.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase literally means little lunch and is their word for the morning meal.

clue.text: Want online lunch? Head round

indicators.note: round means the headland word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness
E is the prefix for electronic or online
to lunch is to dine

explanation.surface: Fancy ordering lunch on the internet? Go and get it yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a verb, but NESS is a headland; it goes 'round' EDINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Want here is the noun for poverty or lack, the state of being in need.

clue.text: With suitable fury, old man returns drink before meal

indicators.note: returns means goes back, so the pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: fit means suitable
ire means anger or fury
pa is a familiar word for father, the old man

explanation.surface: Dad comes home in a fitting rage and wants a drink before dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses FITIREPA as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an alcoholic drink taken to stimulate appetite ahead of eating.

clue.text: Decoration that is on sticker protecting seed

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so the abbreviation follows the rest
protecting means the sticker word wraps around the seed word

parts.note: a paster is one who sticks, a sticker
semen is seed in the reproductive sense
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A decorative label goes on a seed packet to protect it.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived term means ornamental trimming of braid, cord or beads on garments or furniture.

clue.text: How's your father blocking flow from bathroom?

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the way inside the other word

parts.note: to ensue is to follow or flow from
how's your father is British slang for sex, as is it

explanation.surface: Something rude is clogging the drain of the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How's your father' is jokey British slang for sex, like 'it'. 'flow from' belongs to the wordplay, leaving 'bathroom' alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An attached private washroom off a bedroom is commonly called this as a noun.

clue.text: Fancy gear associated with sovereign state

parts.note: sovereign as an adjective means royal, regal
IA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Iowa

explanation.surface: Elaborate costume goes with being a ruling monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign state' reads as one country, but it splits: a royal word plus an American state abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means elaborate ceremonial dress or finery, the fancy outfit worn on state occasions.

clue.text: Pushes horse in front over

indicators.note: in places the horse word inside the reversed piece
over means turned over, so the word for front is read backwards

parts.note: the nose is the front of a car or aircraft
gee-gee is a childish word for a horse, written GG

explanation.surface: A jockey urges on a horse, steering it out in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the word for front backwards before the horse goes in; 'Pushes' is the verb, as in urges.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge someone on is to encourage them forward, so pushes is a fair equivalent.

clue.text: City centre ultimately within borders

indicators.note: within means the letter goes inside the word for borders

parts.note: rims are edges or borders

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word centre

explanation.surface: The city centre lies well inside the boundaries after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Reims is a city in the Champagne region of north-eastern France.

clue.text: Mental unit welcomes positive contribution

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the positive letter goes inside
mental here means crazy, so the letters of unit are scrambled

explanation.surface: A psychiatric unit is glad of anything helpful you can offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mental' rearranges UNIT into INUT, which 'welcomes' P.
explanation.definitionFit: A contribution to discussion or work is commonly called one's input.

clue.text: Heads for Rover garage — genuine new parts going back

indicators.note: parts means separates, so the anagram splits the two initials apart
heads for picks the first letters of the next two words
new signals that the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A Rover garage sources real replacement parts for the car's reverse gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges GENUINE into ENEGUIN, which 'parts' R and G from 'Heads for'. This is the variant spelling of reneging.
explanation.definitionFit: To renege is to go back on a promise, so the participle means going back on one's word.

clue.text: Hull member making special trip to accept award

indicators.note: accept means take in, so the honour sits inside
special signals that the letters are put into an unusual arrangement

parts.note: the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A Hull City player takes a special trip to collect an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hull' suggests the English city, but it is a ship's hull. 'special' rearranges TRIP TO into TOPTIR, which takes MBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-timbers are the uppermost frame pieces of a wooden ship's side, members of its hull.

clue.text: Clay, silt and earth seen in passing

indicators.note: seen in means the earth letter appears within the other word

parts.note: passing can mean death, a loss
E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: Soil types noticed in passing on a walk.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a fine wind-blown loamy deposit, a soil between clay and silt.

clue.text: Produced nothing before the signal to stop

parts.note: FA is short for sweet FA, British slang for nothing at all
a red light signals traffic to stop

explanation.surface: Nothing was made before the stop light came on.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweet FA is British slang for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To have sired a child is to have produced offspring.

clue.text: Arts graduate is running fashion house

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: A graduate in arts is managing a couture business.
explanation.definitionFit: French for house, used in English for a couture firm such as a Paris label.
